findings.text: Provides a boolean isolation service for driver-managed movable pages. Success requires a valid folio backing, presence of the movable-operations marker, exclusive acquisition of the folio lock, absence of a prior isolated marker, availability of driver operations, and acceptance by the driver isolation callback, after which the core marks the page isolated.

Isolation serializes against concurrent compaction, migration and release by taking the folio lock with a non-blocking attempt before any isolation step and holding it across verification and the driver callback. All outcomes release the lock when taken and drop the entry reference, including the race where the page is freed underneath.

Movable-operations identity persists from allocation until free, allowing a pre-lock flag test without disturbing the owner. The isolated marker is owned by the memory core, warned against when preexisting or set by the driver, and set by the core only after driver acceptance.
Always-available advice identifiers include MADV_DOFORK, MADV_DONTFORK, MADV_NORMAL, MADV_SEQUENTIAL, MADV_RANDOM, MADV_REMOVE, MADV_WILLNEED and MADV_DONTNEED.

Always-available advice identifiers further include MADV_DONTNEED_LOCKED, MADV_FREE, MADV_COLD, MADV_PAGEOUT, MADV_POPULATE_READ, MADV_POPULATE_WRITE, MADV_DONTDUMP, MADV_DODUMP, MADV_WIPEONFORK and MADV_KEEPONFORK.

Additional valid identifiers are MADV_GUARD_INSTALL and MADV_GUARD_REMOVE unconditionally, MADV_MERGEABLE and MADV_UNMERGEABLE with same-page merging, MADV_HUGEPAGE, MADV_NOHUGEPAGE and MADV_COLLAPSE with transparent huge pages, and MADV_SOFT_OFFLINE and MADV_HWPOISON with memory-failure support.
Remote vector advice permits only MADV_COLD, MADV_PAGEOUT, MADV_WILLNEED and MADV_COLLAPSE; every other behavior is invalid against a foreign address space.

Hardware poison and soft offline denote a memory-failure injection path that bypasses normal locking and traversal. Without memory-failure support the classifier is uniformly negative and injection completes trivially with success.

Lock selection is behavior driven. Failure injection uses no lock. Removal, willneed, cold, pageout, collapse and both populate directions use the address-space read lock. Guard install and remove with discard-style hints use deferred per-VMA read locking. Remaining behaviors use the killable address-space write lock. Central locks are released centrally with mode reset, while per-VMA and no-lock modes have no central release.
Batched address-translation collection is armed only for MADV_DONTNEED, MADV_DONTNEED_LOCKED and MADV_FREE; all other behaviors skip both setup and teardown of the batch.
User ranges require a page-aligned start and a page-rounded length. Empty-after-rounding from nonzero input and arithmetic wrap of start plus length are invalid.

Only read and write populate directions use the populate path; other behaviors use the VMA walk. Failure injection acts on the raw range without untagging or plugging, while normal paths untag the start for local versus remote context, page-align the length, and hold a block plug across the operation.

Per-VMA read locking is sufficient only for a range ending inside one VMA of the caller own space with no armed userfaultfd and without missing anonymous state. Guard install alone can create the anonymous-state need. The fast path attempts RCU VMA acquisition at the start and otherwise falls back to the address-space read lock with mode updated.

Exposes an RCU-protected lookup that returns a read-locked VMA containing a given address in a given address space, or null when absent, mismatched, or unobtainable. Detachment races are retried internally from the map.

VMA read acquisition pairs a pre-check of the VMA sequence against the address-space sequence with a limited refcount increment using acquire ordering, followed by ownership validation and a second sequence check with acquire semantics ordered against write-side release. False locked outcomes from sequence wrap are possible, false unlocked outcomes are not.

Concurrent VMA free, replacement and migration to another address space are tolerated. Detached entries request map retry, unobtainable references report abort for accounting, mismatched address coverage releases the lock and reports absence, and cross-space attachment holds the other space across the refcount drop to avoid use after free.

Exposes range traversal over VMAs for an advice descriptor, handling a single-VMA fast path under per-VMA locking and otherwise iterating successive VMAs while updating the current subrange and cached neighbors.

Traversal starts with an optional single-VMA attempt, then locates the first overlapping VMA. Gaps before a VMA record a mapping error yet continue from the next VMA start. Per-VMA errors abort immediately. A dropped address-space lock discards cached VMA references, and VMA split or merge extends the subrange before advancing until the original end is reached.

Exposes single-range advice on an explicit address space. It validates the behavior identifier, rejects misaligned or wrapping ranges and empty lengths, acquires the behavior lock, brackets execution with batched translation-cache setup and teardown, runs the behavior, then releases the lock and returns the outcome.
System entry for single-range advice applied to the caller address space with start, length and behavior arguments, delegating to the single-range implementation.

Vector advice holds one lock and translation batch across many segments. Each segment is validated independently. A restart request without fatal signals drops the batch and lock, reacquires them, and retries the same segment; fatal signals convert to interruption. The return is bytes consumed when progress occurred, otherwise the last error.

System entry for vector advice on a task referenced by a process descriptor. It enforces zero flags, imports the vector, resolves task and address space with read-mode ptrace permission, validates behavior and remote constraints, delegates to vector handling, and releases task, space and vector references.

Foreign-space manipulation beyond the caller is limited to the narrow remote behavior subset and requires a system niceness privilege; same-space calls bypass both checks. Read-mode ptrace credential verification avoids leaking address-layout metadata through behavior differences.

Anonymous VMA names allow at most eighty bytes including termination and accept only printable ASCII excluding backslash, backtick, dollar and both square brackets. A null user pointer clears the name.

Exposes anonymous VMA naming over a page-aligned range with page-rounded length, rejecting wrap and empty-after-rounding while treating empty ranges as success. It copies and validates a bounded user name, applies it through behavior-locked VMA traversal under an internal naming behavior, and releases the allocated name.

Exposes bounded duplication of user memory. Length is measured against a caller limit with empty or inaccessible input and over-limit length reported distinctly, allocation failure reported separately, exact measured bytes copied with fault reported and freed on failure, and the final byte forced to termination for the string variant.
Write-protect walk carrier holds a notifier range descriptor, a flush start offset, a flush end offset, and a total count of converted entries.
Cleaning walk extends the base carrier with a bitmap base offset, a bitmap pointer, and start and end page offsets bounding dirty positions, reachable from the base through container linkage.

Scanning converts writable entries to write-protected and dirty entries to clean through paired modify-protect transactions. Each conversion expands the flush interval to cover the page and increments the total; cleaning also sets the corresponding bitmap position and widens the dirty span.
Permission-bit updates use a start then commit pairing scoped to the owning VMA and address, so write-protect and clean transitions apply atomically within the walk.
Huge page-middle-directory entries are never split by these scanners. Trans-huge entries continue without descent, with a warning when such an entry appears writable or dirty.
